extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of PARI/GP (mathematicians and library programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on using and programming PARI/GP: function call syntax, optional arguments and flags, type conventions, conversions, and specific operator/function behaviours in the PARI/GP calculator and library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customizing readline key bindings via .inputrc
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a file named .inputrc in your home directory to change default readline bindings; can include conditionals for gp ($if Pari-GP ... $endif).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example settings: set show-all-if-ambiguous, remap backspace to backward-delete-char, bind sequences like "\C-xd". Use C-x C-r to re-read the init file during a session. Embedding conditional (e.g. $if Pari-GP) allows gp-specific bindings. Note: some bindings can be annoying when copy-pasting (examples given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electric parentheses automatic matching
rubrics_metrics.description: By default ( and [ are bound to pari-matched-insert which can auto-insert the matching closure when electric parentheses are enabled (default off).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Toggle electric behavior by giving numeric argument -2 to '(' (M--2()). Use M--0 / M--1 to specifically switch it off/on if you don't want a toggle. Useful to disable when copy-pasting text into the calculator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Meta/Alt key encoding in readline
rubrics_metrics.description: In some readline versions the Alt/Meta key may produce 8-bit accented characters; you can change behaviour via .inputrc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not want to fall back to the Esc combination, put: set convert-meta on; set output-meta off in .inputrc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command completion and online help behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Hitting <TAB> attempts context-dependent completion; repeated <TAB> lists possible completions. M-h gives short help for the word under cursor, M-H yields extended help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion is context-aware (e.g. after ~ expect username, after default( expect a default keyword, after '.' expect member keyword). If only one completion is meaningful, gp inserts it and may add comma for defaults or parentheses for function names; hitting <TAB> again can show argument list. Example: def<TAB>se<TAB>10 can yield default(seriesprecision,10). None of the help keys disturb the line being edited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using PariEmacs to run gp in Emacs
rubrics_metrics.description: Install PariEmacs and autoload gp modes in your .emacs to run gp as subprocess inside Emacs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include provided autoload lines and add (cons '("\\.gp$" . gp-script-mode) auto-mode-alist) so .gp files open in gp-script-mode. Then M-x gp starts a gp shell with editor facilities. See PariEmacs docs for further customizations and menus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function preconditions and minimal sanity checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Many routines list explicit preconditions (e.g., p is prime); PARI/GP trusts user input and performs only minimal sanity checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preconditions are not met, consequences include regular exceptions, PARI stack overflow, SIGSEGV/SIGBUS, infinite loops, or meaningless results — 'junk in, junk out'. Be careful to satisfy preconditions for safety and correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function documentation and prototype conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are of the form: foo(x, {flag = 0}): short description. Library syntax is shown separately (GEN foo(...)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Braces denote optional arguments. The library prototype shows exact argument types. Optional arguments at the end and in order of decreasing usefulness so defaults are usually ignored. foo() on a function with all optional args yields defaults. A trailing star ({x}*) means any number of such args are accepted (used e.g. by print routines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional arguments and empty-argument trick
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional arguments can be omitted; a comma or closing parenthesis where an optional argument should be signals default. You may use empty arguments to set a later argument while keeping earlier defaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: foo({x=1},{y=2},{z=3}) — typing foo(6,4) gives foo(6,4,3). To set z only: foo(6,,1) yields foo(6,2,1). In rare case where no mandatory args, you can omit parentheses (standalone foo), but not recommended in scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag argument types and mnemonic usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Flags are either generic (explicit numeric values described) or binary (bits represent toggles). Mnemonics (strings) may replace numeric flags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary flags are described as bits mapping to named toggles. Instead of numeric flags, use strings like "Parametric; no Recursive" or "Parametric | no Recursive". For generic flags you can use either numeric (1) or mnemonic "AGM" if documented. Mnemonics are less error-prone and more readable; numeric flags are quicker to type in gp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pointer (&) parameter semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: A parameter prefixed with & in prototypes (foo(x, &e)) means the function may assign a value to e as a side effect; in library calls the & must be typed explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of v2.9.5 pointer arguments are optional for documented functions and will appear in prototypes between brackets as {&e}. In library (GEN) calls, pass &e when you want the side effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library function argument mandatory-ness and default encoding
rubrics_metrics.description: When programming with the PARI library, functions generally accept only mandatory arguments; defaults are encoded (NULL pointer or -1 etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library functions usually have variants for different flag values; use the library's prototype to see how to encode missing arguments. The manual includes an = default token in prototypes to signal how a missing argument should be encoded for the library (often NULL or -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator type compatibility and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetic operators (+, -, *, /, etc.) have type-dependent behaviours and disallow operations between incompatible types or sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: addition between scalar x and t_COL/t_MAT y returns [y[1]+x,...] and y + xId respectively; other additions/subtractions between incompatible vector/matrix sizes are forbidden. Multiplication is not commutative in general due to matrix/vector types. Multiplication between two t_VECs is not allowed; for scalar product transpose one vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division, Euclidean quotient, and remainder semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: / returns exact quotient (e.g., integer division yields rational), x \ y is Euclidean quotient (floor/ceil depending on sign), x \/ y is rounded Euclidean quotient, and x % y is modular Euclidean remainder with type-dependent behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To get approximate real quotient of two integers add 0.; for p-adic add O(p^k); for Taylor series add O(X^k) or use taylor. x%y differs depending on types: for non-integral real numbers x%y = x - (x\y)*y; if y integer, smallest non-negative integer congruent to x mod y; if y polynomial, polynomial of smallest degree congruent to x modulo y. Note promotion rules when mixing polynomials/integers and componentwise application on vectors/matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powering behaviour by exponent type and inverse behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: x^n uses different semantics depending on n: integer exponent uses exact binary-powering, non-integer uses exp(n log x) (componentwise), rational exponents on Mod/p-adic attempt to solve y^q = x^p, negative integer exponents compute inverses and may fail revealing nontrivial factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exponent is rational p/q and x is Mod or p-adic, returns y s.t. y^q = x^p if exists (q must not have large prime factors); non-integer exponent acts componentwise on vectors/matrices. Inverse failures for non-invertible t_INTMOD or t_POLMOD can expose factors of modulus, helpful for factor discovery. Matrix x^(-1) returns a left inverse if one exists for rectangular full-column-rank matrices. Underlying algorithms assume base ring is a domain; failure modes are noted and alternatives (e.g., work with 2-adics or use inversemod workaround) are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: cmp and lex comparison semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: cmp(x,y) returns -1/0/1 using a universal transitive order (0 iff x === y); lex(x,y) gives lexicographic comparison recursively. Length and complexity affect ordering: longer considered larger; when equal lengths, matrix > vector > scalar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: cmp is useful for sorted lists (vecsort(v, cmp) ~ Set(v)). Examples: cmp(1,1.0) = -1 (1==1.0 but not identical). lex compares recursively; examples given. The operator === tests identity strictly (different type/length never identical). The operator == is liberal: many objects considered equal (0, 0 polynomial, zero-vector). Strings (t_STR) compared lexicographically; comparing strings to other types raises exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: divrem behaviour and differences with %
rubrics_metrics.description: divrem(x,y,{v}) returns a column vector [x\y, x - (x\y)*y] (Euclidean quotient and remainder). This is not the same as x % y in many cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use divrem when you need both quotient and remainder without two divisions. If v present and x,y are multivariate polynomials, divide wrt variable v. Examples show divrem(1/2,3)[2] = 1/2 while (1/2)%3 = 2. Some combinations can be illegal (e.g., Mod with integer divisor) and will raise errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: vecmax/vecmin semantics and optional index pointer
rubrics_metrics.description: vecmax(x,{&v}) returns largest entry of vector/matrix x (or copy of x if not container); vecmin analogous. If &v present, it is set to index (or [i,j] for matrix) of an extreme entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Error if x is empty. For vectors &v yields index of largest/smallest entry; for matrices &v yields coordinates [i,j]. If x is not vector/matrix the pointer is ignored. Examples provided (vecmax([10,20,-30,40], &v) yields 40 and v=4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard comparison and boolean operators behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard operators <=, <, >=, >, ==, != are available returning 1 for true and 0 for false; === tests strict identity. Boolean operators ||, &&, ! available. GP accepts <> as synonym for !=. = is assignment, not equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: == is liberal (e.g., integer 0, 0 polynomial, zero-vector test equal). === is strict: objects of different type/length never identical. Comparing t_STR to other types raises exception. Use identity vs equality appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Col(x,{n}) conversion to column vector rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Col transforms x into a column vector; optional n sets dimension. Default behaviour depends on x type (most objects produce 1-component vector; vectors/quadratic forms treated as row vectors; polynomials/power series produce coefficient vectors with leading coefficient first; matrices and strings produce special conversions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: n omitted or 0 -> dimension depends on type. If n given, appends zeros if n>0, prepends zeros if n<0; dimension of result is |n|. For matrix and character string, n is meaningless and must be omitted or an error is raised. Reciprocal of Pol and Ser is Vec in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colrev(x,{n}) conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Colrev acts as Col(x, -n) then reverse the result. Colrev is reciprocal of Polrev: coefficients start with constant term and increase by degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want coefficient ordering starting at constant term. Library variants available as gtocolrev0 and gtocolrev.

rubrics_metrics.name: List({x = []}) conversion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms a row or column vector x into a list of entries; for other types creates a singleton list; omitted x creates an empty list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except when x omitted, this function creates a small memory leak—initialize lists to empty or use sparingly. Library syntax: gtolist; mklist creates empty list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map({x}) associative-array conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Map converts a 2-column matrix [a1,b1; ... ; an,bn] to an associative map ai -> bi. With no argument creates empty map fillable via mapput.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to convert factor lists (example: Map(factor(13!)); mapget(M,3) returns 5). Library syntax: gtomap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mat({x = []}) conversion to matrix rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Mat transforms x into a matrix. If x already matrix, returns a copy. If x row/column vector creates 1-row/1-column matrix unless elements are column/row vectors of same length then concatenates. Binary quadratic forms produce 2x2 matrix; otherwise creates 1x1 matrix containing x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For some inputs n is meaningless. Examples illustrate various conversions. Library syntax: gtomat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mod(a,b) modular object creation and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Mod(a,b) creates intmod or polmod objects (t_INTMOD/t_POLMOD) representing a mod b. If a%b yields appropriate type, Mod succeeds as well; complex objects are base-changed to Z/bZ or K[x]/(b) for efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mod objects can be lifted via lift or centerlift; modulus recovered via z.mod. Mod(a,b) is different from x%y which has no knowledge of modulus: Mod(4,5)+1 = Mod(0,5) while 4%5 + 1 = 5. Use Mod when working in a modular ring for consistent behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pol(t,{v}) and Polrev(t,{v}) polynomial conversions and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Pol transforms t into polynomial with main variable v. For vectors it creates polynomial with t[1] leading coefficient; Polrev uses t[1] as constant term. Not a substitution function: variable priority matters and may raise error if variable priority is wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pol is efficient for creating polynomials from coefficient vectors (linear vs naive quadratic evaluation). Use Vec/Vecrev as reciprocals. Warning: Pol(x+y,y) fails since variable must have higher priority; use appropriate variable ordering or conversion functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ser(s,{v},{d}) power series conversion and precision behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Ser transforms s into power series in variable v with precision d (seriesprecision default). For scalars/polynomials behaves like multiplication by 1+O(v^d); for vectors, vector coefficients give series coefficients starting at constant term and d is ignored (unless convert/truncate to t_POL first).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If s already a power series in v, Ser returns it verbatim ignoring d. To obtain a certain number of significant terms when input is vector or existing series, convert/truncate to polynomial first. Examples show when d is ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set({x = []}) conversion to set rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Set converts x to a row vector with strictly increasing entries according to universal cmp; container types converted elementwise; other types become single-element set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Set([1,2,4,2,1,3]) -> [1,2,3,4]. Useful to canonicalize lists/vectors; library syntax gtoset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Str({x}*) and related string conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Str concatenates arguments into a single t_STR string; arguments evaluated in string context. Strchr converts integer to single character; Strexpand performs environment expansion on string; Strtex translates arguments to TeX format and concatenates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use eval on a string to recover a GEN (eval(Str(x,i))). Str creates a malloced string in library mode via GENtostr/strtoGEN pair; free when done. Strexpand can be used to read environment variables (e.g., "$HOME/doc").

rubrics_metrics.name: Vec(x,{n}), Vecrev, and Vecsmall conversion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Vec transforms x into a row vector; behavior depends on x type (polynomial -> coefficient vector starting with leading coefficient; matrix -> vector of columns; map -> domain vector; string -> vector of characters). Vecrev returns reversed Vec (or Vec(x,-n) then reverse). Vecsmall returns a t_VECSMALL when representable as vector of small integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If n omitted dimension depends on type; if n given zeros appended/prepended. For some input types (matrix, string, map, error) n is meaningless. Use Vecsmall for ASCII conversions of strings to small integer vectors. Library variants available with suffix 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: binary(x) conversion to binary digits
rubrics_metrics.description: binary(x) outputs vector of binary digits of |x|. For reals produces two components (integer part and fractional part as digits); for vectors/matrices applied componentwise. By convention 0 has no digits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example binary(10) -> [1,0,1,0]; binary(0) -> []. Useful for bit-level inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitand(x,y) bitwise AND semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: bitand(x,y) computes bitwise AND of two integers (xi and yi)2^i summed. Negative numbers behave 2-adically: result is 2-adic limit of bitand(xn,yn) for non-negative approximants; result is ordinary integer possibly negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: bitand(5,3)=1; bitand(-5,3)=3; bitand(-5,-3)=-7. Library syntax gbitand; ibitand returns bitwise and of |x| and |y|.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitneg(x,{n}) bitwise negation (truncated)
rubrics_metrics.description: bitneg performs bitwise negation of integer x truncated to n bits (n >= 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition and precise formula given in manual (entry is truncated here). Use with n to limit negation width; when n omitted default behaviour described in manual.
